instructions.name: accept_config_authority
docs: Completes a proposed `Config.authority` transfer.

instructions.name: accept_marketplace_authority
docs: Completes a proposed `Marketplace.authority` transfer.

instructions.name: add_stake
docs: Locks `amount` of additional collateral into the seller's
`stake_vault`.

instructions.name: close_dispute
docs: Permissionless once a complaint is decided and its receipt is too
old to reuse. Deletes the record and refunds its rent to the
buyer.

accounts.name: buyer
docs: bound to `dispute.buyer` via `has_one` below.

instructions.name: expire_dispute
docs: Permissionless once a complaint has sat undecided for 30 days.
Nobody is paid, the bond returns to the buyer, the permit's freeze
lifts, and the marketplace takes a public mark.

instructions.name: grant_permit
docs: Creates the seller's `SlashPermit` for a marketplace, locking
`max_slashable` out of their free collateral and freezing the
marketplace's current `complaint_window`/`bond_bps` onto it.

instructions.name: increase_permit
docs: Adds `delta` to an existing permit's `max_slashable`. Increase-only:
there is no handler that lowers a cap.

instructions.name: initialize_config
docs: Pins the protocol's collateral mint and chain tag, and records the
caller as the first `Config.authority`. Only the compiled-in
initial admin may call this.

accounts.name: mint
docs: The protocol-wide collateral mint, pinned by address. There is no
`update_config`, so a deployment that pins the wrong mint here can
only be replaced, never repaired. Which extensions it may carry is
checked in [`handler`], where the allow-list can be named in the
error.

instructions.name: initialize_stake
docs: Creates a seller's one-and-only `SellerStake` account and its
`stake_vault`. Moves no collateral; `add_stake` does that.

instructions.name: propose_config_authority
docs: Names a new `Config.authority`. Takes effect only once the named
key accepts.

instructions.name: propose_marketplace_authority
docs: Names a new `Marketplace.authority`. Takes effect only once the
named key accepts.

instructions.name: raise_dispute
docs: Opens a complaint about `order_id`, proved by a
marketplace-signed receipt that the transaction's Ed25519
instruction verifies. Must be submitted as
`[Ed25519Program verify, raise_dispute]`, in that order.

accounts.name: config
docs: Carried for `chain_id` alone, which is the one receipt field with
no account of its own to check against.

accounts.name: dispute
docs: The replay guard: a second complaint about the same order collides
with this address and `init` fails (docs/DESIGN-v2.md, "The
offchain receipt").

accounts.name: instructions_sysvar
docs: `ed25519::verify_signed_receipt`, which is the first thing the
handler does. Left unchecked here rather than carrying an
`address` constraint so that the module which reads this account
is also the module that proves it is the right one.

instructions.name: register_marketplace
docs: Registers a new marketplace tenant and creates its `bond_vault`.

instructions.name: release_permit
docs: Permissionless once `now >= revoked_at + complaint_window` and
`open_disputes == 0`. Subtracts the permit's remaining allowance
from `stake.committed`, closes the permit, and refunds its rent to
the seller.

accounts.name: seller
docs: bound to `permit.seller` via `has_one` below.

instructions.name: release_permit_early
docs: Does what `release_permit` does but skips the wait when both the
seller and the marketplace's current authority sign.

instructions.name: resolve_dispute
docs: Decides an open complaint. Signed by the marketplace's arbiter.
Upheld pays the buyer out of the seller's collateral and returns
the bond; rejected forfeits the bond to the seller.

instructions.name: revoke_permit
docs: Stamps `revoked_at`, starting the permit's complaint window. Frees
no collateral by itself; `release_permit` does that once the
window elapses.

instructions.name: update_marketplace
docs: Updates whichever of a marketplace's settings are supplied; the
rest keep their current value.

instructions.name: withdraw_stake
docs: Moves `amount` out of the seller's `stake_vault`, gated on
`staked - amount >= committed`.

types.name: Config
docs: Network-wide settings, one PDA per deployment (`["config", "v2"]`).
`collateral_mint` and `chain_id` are fixed at `initialize_config` and
never change: there is no `update_config`, since changing the mint once
vaults hold tokens would strand every balance, and the chain tag is a
deployment fact. Only `authority` moves, through the two-step transfer.

types.name: DisputeExpired
docs: The marketplace's permanent public mark for never deciding
(decision 7). Nobody is paid; the bond goes back to the buyer.

types.name: DisputeRecord
docs: An open or resolved complaint (`["dispute", "v2", marketplace, seller,
order_id]`), created by `raise_dispute` and deleted by `close_dispute`
once its receipt is too old to reuse. The account's existence is also
the replay guard: a second complaint against the same order collides
with this PDA and cannot be created.

fields.name: bond
docs: The amount actually deposited, not recomputed later from a
possibly-changed `bond_bps`.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: `created_at + DISPUTE_EXPIRY` (30 days, protocol constant).

fields.name: closable_after
docs: `receipt.issued_at + max(permit.complaint_window,
MAX_COMPLAINT_WINDOW_SECONDS)`, not the live permit's own window
alone: a permit PDA carries no nonce, so a grandfathered
marketplace's wider window must not let a re-grant at the same
address outlive the record that blocks its own receipts from being
replayed (`raise_dispute`'s handler doc comment; docs/DESIGN-v2.md).

fields.name: status
docs: One of [`DisputeStatus`], as `DisputeStatus::Open as u8`.

types.name: DisputeResolved
docs: Carries the buyer and the outcome, which is what makes a buyer's
history computable offchain without storing any of it onchain
(docs/DESIGN-v2.md, "What this design deliberately does not do").
`payout` is zero on the rejected path, where the bond moves to the
seller instead.

types.name: Marketplace
docs: A tenant of the protocol (`["market", "v2", marketplace_id]`).
`marketplace_id` is the client-chosen, immutable identity every
subordinate PDA derives from; `authority`, `receipt_signer` and
`arbiter` are ordinary fields that rotate through `update_marketplace`
and the two-step authority transfer, so a lost or rotated key never
orphans a seller's permit or the dispute history.

fields.name: prev_receipt_signer
docs: Valid for receipts issued before `signer_rotated_at`, so an honest
key rotation doesn't silently void every outstanding buyer's claim.

fields.name: complaint_window
docs: 2..30 days. Copied onto each new permit at grant time (Phase 2).

fields.name: bond_bps
docs: <= `MAX_BOND_BPS`. Copied onto each new permit at grant time (Phase 2).

types.name: SellerStake
docs: A seller's shared collateral, one PDA per seller globally
(`["stake", "v2", seller]`), backing every marketplace they sell on.
`initialize_stake` creates this account and its `stake_vault` only;
`add_stake` moves collateral. That split is what lets a seller slashed
to zero call `add_stake` and trade again, rather than being stuck with
a permanently dead account.

fields.name: staked
docs: Always equal to `stake_vault`'s token balance.

fields.name: committed
docs: Sum of REMAINING allowance across active permits, that is
`max_slashable - slashed` summed over every unreleased
`SlashPermit` (Phase 2). Defined as the sum of caps would break
`committed <= staked` the first time anyone is slashed.

types.name: SlashPermit
docs: A seller's bounded, revocable line of credit to one marketplace
(`["permit", "v2", seller, marketplace]`). Declared now because
docs/DESIGN-v2.md's account model fixes all five account layouts
together; no handler creates or reads this until `grant_permit`
(Phase 2).

fields.name: max_slashable
docs: Increase-only: the seller can raise this but never lower it.

fields.name: open_disputes
docs: Blocks release of THIS permit only.

fields.name: revoked_at
docs: `i64::MAX` means active. A zero sentinel would make the release
check trivially true for every active permit.

fields.name: complaint_window
docs: Frozen at grant from the marketplace's setting at that moment.

fields.name: bond_bps
docs: Frozen at grant from the marketplace's setting at that moment.

fields.name: granted_at
docs: Stamped from `Clock` in `grant_permit`, never touched again
(`increase_permit` modifies this same era, it does not start a new
one). Together with `revoked_at` this bounds the era a receipt has
to fall inside: a permit PDA is freed by both release paths and
re-granted at the same address, so a receipt has to be checked
against the era that actually issued it, not merely against
whatever occupies the address now (`raise_dispute`, check 7).
Appended here, after `bond_bps`, because it was added after those
fields already shipped: Borsh is positional, so a field this
struct's account-model rule requires be appended, not inserted,
must sit immediately before `reserved`, in the order the fields
were actually introduced.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Shrunk from 32 to 24 bytes to make room for `granted_at` above:
this is exactly the layout evolution `reserved` exists for (see
the account-model note in docs/DESIGN-v2.md), and using it keeps
every `SlashPermit`'s size, and therefore its rent, unchanged.
